kaikki_vikisozluk.e: فَتْوَى • (fatwā) f (plural فَتَاوَى (fatāwā) or فَتَاوٍ (fatāwin, construct state فَتَاوِي (fatāwī)))
kaikki_vikisozluk.t: From Classical Syriac ܦܬܘܐ (peṯwā, “spinning out, breadth (of words)”), with some details in the sectarian semantics of Late Antiquity Aramaic crossed with Arabic, that led to the present specification, now being obscure. أَفْتَى (ʔaftā, “to deliver a formal opinion”) was parallelly borrowed.
s: Classical Syriac ܦܬܘܐ (peṯwā, “spinning out, breadth (of words)”)

kaikki_vikisozluk.e: أَفْتَى • (ʔaftā) IV (non-past يُفْتِي (yuftī), verbal noun إِفْتَاء (ʔiftāʔ))
kaikki_vikisozluk.t:
Etymology tree
Proto-West Semitic *pataw-der.
Classical Syriac ܐܦܬܝ (ʾap̄tī)bor.
Arabic أفتى
From Classical Syriac ܐܦܬܝ (ʾap̄tī, “to expand; to propagate (orthodoxy)”), which is a causative to Proto-West Semitic *pataw- (“to penetrate”), perhaps also encompassing idioms such as Akkadian 𒊻𒉆 𒉿𒌅𒌑𒌝 (uznam petûm), 𒊻𒉆 𒁍𒌓𒌅𒌝 (uznam puttûm, literally “to open an ear”), from the related *pataḥ- (“to open”), so it would be equivalent to Arabic فَتَحَ أُذْنًا (fataḥa ʔuḏnan).
The corresponding noun فَتْوَى (fatwā, “formal opinion”) has its patterning reflecting Classical Syriac ܦܬܘܐ (peṯwā, “spinning out, breadth (of words)”).

Proto-West Semitic *pataw-der.
Classical Syriac ܐܦܬܝ (ʾap̄tī)bor.
Arabic أفتى
